title: Diagnose an SDDC Manager failure from events and support-bundle logs
prompt:
Implement `vcf_failure_diagnostics/client.py` as a standard-library-only VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC Manager integration. The supplied incident is deliberately non-diagnostic at the Task level: its FAILED task contains a generic error and a `referenceToken`. Your implementation must retrieve and correlate the relevant Notifications and collect the requested SOS support-bundle logs. Do not guess a root cause from the task message.

Before implementing, research the SDDC Manager OpenAPI specification in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. Confirm the `getTask`, `getNotifications`, `startSupportBundle`, `getSupportBundleStatus`, and `exportSupportBundleByID` operations and cite the specification URLs consulted.

Keep the public exports declared by `vcf_failure_diagnostics/__init__.py`:

- `SupportBundleSelection(domain_name, *, cluster_names=None, sddc_manager_logs=None, nsx_logs=None, api_logs=None, include_free_hosts=None, force=None, summary_report=None)` is an immutable request model. `domain_name` and every supplied cluster name must be non-blank strings; a whitespace-only value is a `ValueError`. The log, scope, and option switches must be booleans when supplied. `to_wire()` uses the exact OpenAPI camelCase properties. `None` means unset and must omit the property completely; do not send null, an empty string, an empty object, or a placeholder. An explicitly supplied empty `cluster_names` sequence is different from `None` and must remain `clusterNames: []`; an explicit `False` switch must remain false. Omit `options` when both option values are unset, and do not manufacture properties that the caller did not supply.
- `SddcManagerClient(base_url, access_token, *, sleep=time.sleep, poll_interval=1.0, max_polls=20, timeout=10.0)` uses only Python standard-library modules. Treat `base_url` as an HTTP(S) origin: reject embedded credentials, query, fragment, or a non-root path. Disable environment proxies and redirects. Validate all construction arguments locally.
- `diagnose_failed_task(task_id, selection) -> dict` owns the evidence workflow. Validate its arguments before traffic; a blank or whitespace-only `task_id` is a `ValueError`. Fetch `getTask` first and require a JSON Task whose `id` matches and whose status is exactly `FAILED`. Require exactly one non-empty error `referenceToken`, valid creation and completion timestamps, and at least one non-empty task resource ID. Then fetch `getNotifications`. A relevant event is a Notification whose timestamp is inclusively within the task interval and whose `resources` contains one of the task resource IDs. Preserve every complete relevant Notification in server order; absence of relevant events is an evidence error.
- Start the support bundle with exactly `selection.to_wire()`. A 202 response is acceptance only: take its non-empty `id` and always call `getSupportBundleStatus`, even if the acceptance body claims completion. Poll at most `max_polls` status GETs. `PENDING` and `IN_PROGRESS` are nonterminal; call the injected sleep only between nonterminal polls and never after the final allowed poll. `COMPLETED_WITH_SUCCESS` permits download; `COMPLETED_WITH_FAILURE` is an evidence error; a missing or unknown status, mismatched ID, or malformed body raises the corresponding exported error; an exhausted poll budget raises `PollTimeoutError` carrying `bundle_id`, `max_polls`, and `last_status` attributes. Download only through `exportSupportBundleByID` after successful completion.
- Treat the downloaded octet stream as a gzip-compressed tar archive in memory; never extract it to disk. Inspect regular `.log` members as UTF-8 text. Parse each regular `.log` member as one complete UTF-8 JSON document and traverse nested objects recursively. The diagnostic evidence is the unique task object whose `id` exactly matches the failed Task and whose nested `errors` contains an object with the exact `referenceToken` and non-empty string `errorCode` and `message` values. Missing or ambiguous matching evidence is an `EvidenceError`; never substitute the task or notification wording.
- Return exactly `{"taskId": ..., "taskStatus": "FAILED", "referenceToken": ..., "supportBundleId": ..., "rootCause": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "logPath": ...}, "events": [...]}`. Values must come from the retrieved evidence; `logPath` is the matching tar member name and `events` contains the intact relevant Notification dictionaries.

Wire behavior is part of the deliverable. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on all five operations. Send `Accept: application/json` on JSON operations and `Accept: application/octet-stream` on the download. Send compact UTF-8 JSON and `Content-Type: application/json` only on `startSupportBundle`; GETs have no body, no query, and no Content-Type. Percent-encode each path identifier as one path segment. Accept exactly the documented success status for each operation. Non-success responses raise `SddcManagerError` with integer `.status_code` and the decoded JSON object, when available, on `.payload`; exception text and repr must not reveal the bearer token.

Run `python3 -B tests/verify.py`. Edit only `vcf_failure_diagnostics/client.py`.
